name: Daily Offering
overview: The daily offering, as outlined in Exodus 29:38-42, involved the continual sacrifice of two lambs each day—one in the morning and one in the evening—accompanied by a specific measure of flour, oil, and wine as a drink offering. This regular burnt offering was to be made at the tabernacle's entrance as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, symbolizing ongoing dedication and communion with God. Additionally, Exodus 30:7 highlights the ritual of burning sweet incense each morning, further emphasizing the daily, sacrificial nature of worship that foreshadows Christ's ultimate offering.
